text: A song of praise. Of David. I will exalt you, my God and King, and bless your name forever and ever.
Every day I will bless you and praise your name forever and ever.
Great is the LORD, and greatly to be praised; his greatness is beyond all searching out.
One generation will commend your works to the next and tell of your mighty acts.
On the glorious splendor of your majesty, and on the story of your wonderful works, I will meditate.

versions.text: They will speak of the glorious splendor of your majesty, and I will meditate on your wonderful works.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew line has only one verb, אָשִׂיחָה ("I will meditate/ponder"), governing both objects. Introducing "They will speak of" adds a subject and verb not present in the text and splits a single unified line into two.

versions.text: On the glorious splendor of your majesty and on your wonderful works I will meditate.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew has וְדִבְרֵי נִפְלְאוֹתֶיךָ, literally "the words/account of your wonderful deeds," and דִּבְרֵי is currently unrepresented. Rendering it as "the story of your wonderful works" restores the noun while keeping the single verb אָשִׂיחָה governing both objects, as in the current revision. The added commas also help the fronted double object read smoothly aloud. The existing rendering is a defensible simplification, since many render the construct loosely.

text: They will tell of the power of your awesome deeds, and I will proclaim your greatness.
They will celebrate the fame of your abundant goodness and sing aloud of your righteousness.

versions.text: They will pour out the memory of your abundant goodness and sing aloud of your righteousness.
versions.explanation: "Pour out the memory" is awkward when read aloud. זֵכֶר here carries the sense of "fame, renown" and יַבִּיעוּ the sense of bubbling over in celebration, which reads more naturally.

text: The LORD is gracious and merciful, slow to anger and abounding in steadfast love.
The LORD is good to all; his compassion rests on all he has made.
All your works will give you thanks, O LORD, and your faithful ones will bless you.
They will speak of the glory of your kingdom and tell of your power,
to make known to the children of men his mighty acts and the glorious splendor of his kingdom.

versions.text: to make known to all people your mighty acts and the glorious splendor of your kingdom.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew shifts to third person here (גְּבוּרֹתָיו, מַלְכוּתוֹ, "his"), and the object is "the children of men" (בְּנֵי הָאָדָם); "all people" adds "all," which is not in the text.

text: Your kingdom is an everlasting kingdom, and your dominion endures through all generations.
The LORD upholds all who fall and lifts up all who are bowed down.
The eyes of all look to you in hope, and you give them their food at the proper time.
You open your hand and satisfy the desire of every living thing.
The LORD is righteous in all his ways and faithful in all he does.
The LORD is near to all who call on him, to all who call on him in truth.
He fulfills the desire of those who fear him; he hears their cry and saves them.
The LORD watches over all who love him, but all the wicked he will destroy.
My mouth will speak the praise of the LORD, and let all flesh bless his holy name forever and ever.
